briefing.headline: Kestrel's aggressive high press and turnovers haven't produced goals; Harbour have punished central exposures to lead 2-0.

working.text: Kestrel are pressing intensely (PPDA 4.2) and winning the ball very high (turnover height 47.3 m), generating sustained pressure in the opponent’s half.
They have more final-third entries (32) and similar shot volume (8) as Harbour, so the press is creating attacking access even if chances haven’t been converted.

not_working.text: Kestrel’s high defensive line (def line height 38.7 m) and central positioning leave them vulnerable centrally, which Harbour have exploited.
Their intense press may be costly: PPDA 4.2 suggests high physical output that risks fading later (PPDA is much lower than Harbour’s 8).

predictions.claim: Gregor Molina will have Kestrel sit slightly deeper to reduce Harbour’s success through the centre; centre channel entries by Harbour will fall by at least 30%.
To preserve legs and control risk, Kestrel’s PPDA will rise by at least 20% as they ease the intensity of their press.
Kestrel will push to regain territorial edge and increase their final-third entries by at least 20%.

working.text: Harbour have been efficient from central entries — 47.6% of their final-third entries come down the middle — and have scored twice.
They have defended deeper (def line 31.3 m) and conceded high turnovers, which has allowed them to absorb Kestrel’s pressure and counter.

not_working.text: Harbour press much less intensely (PPDA 8) and win the ball lower (turnover height 30.3 m), so they are not matching Kestrel’s ability to create sustained pressure high up.
Their field tilt is low (33.8%), showing they have had less overall possession in the attacking phase despite being clinical.

predictions.claim: Ines Kavanagh will ask Harbour to move the ball more directly and increase progressive passes by at least 15% to exploit Kestrel’s high line on transitions.
Harbour will try to take more of the game into the final third themselves — final-third entries will increase by at least 20% as they look to control the ball higher.
